newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Weak demand keeps S.E.Asian rubber prices soft.
newsitem.headline: Weak demand keeps S.E.Asian rubber prices soft.

text.p: Generally soft regional demand and bumper stocks in Japan may force Southeast Asian rubber prices to head south this week although there could be brief shortcovering rallies in the market, traders said on Monday.
"I think you're going to see some short rallies, but the fundamentals of the market are bearish," a leading trader in a Western commodity house in Singapore said.
Any rally will easily be capped by the buildup of rubber stocks in Japan, which may take months to wind down to an acceptable level, dealers said.
"You've got to get rid of all these stocks in Japan. Those stocks will keep the market from rallying in any significant manner," another dealer said.
In Indonesia, the benchmark SIR20 rubber price will probably move in a narrow range with bargain-hunting likely as prices are considered to have reached bottom, dealers said.
"Bargain-hunting is likely in SIR20, but the impact will probably be limited as overall demand is seen remaining weak," one dealer in the north Sumatran city of Medan said.

Dealers said SIR20 offer prices for November were expected to stay between 55.00-55.50 U.S. cents a lb FOB Medan and at 54.75-55.25 cents FOB Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and at 54.50-55.00 cents FOB Jambi and Pontianak.
Another dealer said supply was not as tight as had been forecast as recent torrential rains fell mostly during the late afternoon and evening and failed to have an impact on tapping.
One latex dealer said latex offer prices would probably stay between 90 to 93 cents a kg, but deals were more likely to be consumated at around 90 cents/kg.
The dealer said he expected to ship around 1,000 tonnes of latex in October to the United States and Spain, but declined to reveal the price of these purchases.
Malaysian rubber prices were also expected to move in a tight range with a downward bias since consumer demand remains soft, traders said.
"I think we might see a fall of about three to five cents," a dealer with a trading house in Kuala Lumpur said.
On Friday, benchmark RSS1 rubber was quoted at Malaysian 313 cents a kg, while SMR20 closed at 305.50 cents.
Another dealer expressed the hope that wet weather expected through the week might help shore up rubber prices.
The supply of raw materials remains ample after a prolonged dry spell last month, but the return of rains last week has made producers cautious of selling at low levels, said traders.
In Thailand, rubber prices moved in a narrow range with a downward bias for the whole week in a listless market, trade sources said.
"There's not much going on in the market. Demand seems to be weak," said one Thai trader.
The benchmark RSS3 rubber for November shipment this week was quoted at around US$1.24-1.26 a kg FOB Bangkok, compared with $1.25 last week, they said.
Prices slid by around 10 percent from the same period last year, an official in the Thai rubber auction market said.
